text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A document proving that Welfare Party -- now in power -- was given $500,000 from Libya in 1989 is in the hands of conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller visits deputies from her party to convince them not to suppport an opposition-led censure motion.
- Conservative deputies from two rival parties held secret meetings for the revival of a right-wing coalition.
- Welfare invites armed forces chief Ismail Hakki Karadayi to their congress at the weekend.
- Hospital chief says 12 million Turks are in need of psychiatric treatment.
- Leftist veteran Bulent Ecevit says he would joint proposed new secularist coalition.
- More than 227 million meters square of land in Istanbul is under the occupation of shanty towns.
- Central bank head does not see any economic crisis in the short term.
- Islamist-led government planning to sell-off 70,000 civil servants lodgings as the first step of selling state-owned estates to raise money.
